Mubadala release (5 Aug 2026; also BusinessWire, TechCrunch, The National, Just Auto the same day): Moove raised $250 million in a Series C at a $2.1 billion valuation, led by Mubadala Investment Company and co-led by Woven Capital (Toyota's growth fund) and Ion Pacific; BlueCrest Capital Management and Sona Capital joined as new investors alongside BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton, Uber, Left Lane, Square Associates, The Latest Ventures and the Ontario Power Generation Pension Plan. Global Fleet and ITWeb Africa, quoting the 5 Aug 2026 release: Moove operates around 42,000 vehicles across 29 cities in 13 countries and reports annual recurring revenue of about $420 million; it has grown organically and through acquisitions including Kovi in Brazil and Tokyo Taxi in Japan.

The National (5 Aug 2026): Moove is a UAE (Dubai-headquartered) mobility company, originally from Lagos.

Jaguar Racing media (Apr 2024) and Jaguar newsroom (Apr 2026): Jaguar TCS Racing has committed to the GEN4 era, Seasons 13-16 through 2030, and revealed its GEN4 prototype in April 2026; Jaguar will have competed in every generation of Formula E.

brief.industry_meta: Mobility Infrastructure · Autonomous & EV Fleet Operations
brief.deck: Moove, the fleet operator that runs Waymo's all-electric Jaguar I-PACE robotaxis in Phoenix and Miami and is Waymo's named partner for London, announced a $250M Series C at a $2.1B valuation on 5 August, led by Mubadala and co-led by Toyota's Woven Capital and Ion Pacific.
brief.the_case_p1: The round is announced by the lead investor and the company: $250M at $2.1B, led by Mubadala, co-led by Woven Capital and Ion Pacific, with BlueCrest and Sona Capital new alongside BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton and Uber. Moove reports about $420M of annual recurring revenue from roughly 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries. Proceeds go to owning autonomous fleets outright and to 'Nests', robotics-first depots where robotaxis are charged, serviced and orchestrated, with the autonomous workforce growing from about 150 to about 500 by year-end.
brief.the_case_p2: The identity moment is the pivot from financing drivers in Lagos to owning the operating layer beneath robotaxis. Since Waymo contracted Moove for Phoenix and Miami in December 2024, every vehicle it runs there has been a Jaguar I-PACE; London, Waymo's first European city, is next, with Moove as fleet partner and service pending regulators. A company about to put its name on driverless Jaguars in three cities needs a brand its riders, regulators and partners recognise.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 5 August and teams close Season 13 rosters this autumn, before the Jeddah opener on 18 December; Moove's two Waymo cities then host the Miami E-Prix on 20 February and the London E-Prix on 29-30 May 2027, and London's driverless launch is due the same season.
brief.why_team_para: Jaguar TCS Racing is the only team whose road car Moove already runs: the Waymo fleets it operates in Phoenix and Miami, and will operate in London, are Jaguar I-PACEs. Jaguar has committed to the GEN4 era through 2030, so the platform outlives a three-year deal. The sponsor table shows TCS as title partner, Castrol and Jaguar itself, and no fleet, mobility or ride-hail partner at Jaguar or on any Formula E roster; the lane is clean and the London E-Prix is the home round.
brief.value_content: MODE B - halo with mechanics. Moove's product, depots and charging orchestration for EV fleets, is not a race-car input, so the value is commercial: Official Fleet Partner, a Jaguar-branded robotaxi story in race weeks at Miami and London, rider-to-race activations, and a demonstrable road-EV use of the I-PACE that the racing programme was built to promote. Moove brings Mubadala, Toyota, Uber and Waymo into the Jaguar suite; the team gives livery, hospitality and driver content.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Fleet Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, spanning the London launch and the fleet-ownership build. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year. Scope: sidepod placement, Miami and London hospitality, co-branded I-PACE fleet livery on race weeks, driver appearances at Nest openings.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Delano co-founded Moove in Lagos in 2020, is Co-CEO and separately chairman, and fronts the raises; he is UK-based. Path: Jide Odunsi, Co-Founder and Co-CEO; Tayo Oyegunle, COO; Tingting Peng, Chief Capital, Strategy and Impact Officer. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the cars Moove already runs.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Ladi, every Waymo you operate in Phoenix and Miami is a Jaguar, and London is next. Jaguar's race team has no fleet partner and its home race is the London E-Prix. 25 minutes before the roster closes to see the numbers?”
score_cells: Round 5 Aug; off-season, but rosters close before the 18 Dec opener.
$250M at $2.1B, $420M ARR; capital is earmarked for fleets.
Runs Jaguar I-PACE fleets; Miami and London map onto rounds.
London launch pending regulators; no hard deadline.
MODE B halo; lane open; product not a race-team input.
risks: Depots and charging orchestration give the team nothing to use; a halo at a manufacturer team can read as a logo.
Anchor the deal on the I-PACE fleets and the two matching rounds; keep the activation about cars, not depots.
The round funds owning autonomous vehicles outright, a capital-intensive plan that competes with marketing spend.
Size the entry small and value-in-kind heavy: fleet livery and rider activations cost Moove little.
brief.bottom_line: A $250M round at $2.1B announced by Mubadala, about $420M of recurring revenue, and Jaguar I-PACE robotaxi fleets in Phoenix, Miami and soon London put Moove at peak brand motive with a unique tie to one team. The lane at Jaguar is open; the halo-only value and fleet capex hold the score at 71.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 5 August Mubadala and Moove announced a $250M Series C at a $2.1B valuation, led by Mubadala Investment Company and co-led by Woven Capital, Toyota's growth fund, and Ion Pacific, with BlueCrest and Sona Capital new alongside BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton, Uber and the Ontario Power Generation Pension Plan. It is a lead-investor release, carried the same day by BusinessWire, TechCrunch and The National.

why_now.label: Scale behind it
why_now.text: Moove reports about $420M of annual recurring revenue from roughly 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries, built organically and through the acquisitions of Kovi in Brazil and Tokyo Taxi in Japan. The proceeds fund autonomous fleet ownership and 'Nests', robotics-first depots where robotaxis are charged, serviced and orchestrated, with the autonomous workforce growing from about 150 to about 500 by the end of 2026.

why_now.label: The London launch
why_now.text: Waymo named Moove its fleet partner for London in October 2025, its first European city, operating and maintaining all-electric Jaguar I-PACEs; testing is under way under a government-backed pilot and commercial service is pending regulatory approval. A brand launching driverless Jaguars in London wants to be known there before the cars arrive.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December and teams close rosters this autumn. The Miami E-Prix on 20 February and the London E-Prix double-header on 29-30 May 2027 are Moove's two Waymo cities; the Austin E-Prix on 6 February adds a third US stage.

why_team.label: The cars Moove runs
why_team.text: Waymo's Phoenix and Miami fleets that Moove operates and maintains are all-electric Jaguar I-PACEs, and the London fleet will be too. No other team on either grid has its road car in Moove's daily operation.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Per the sponsor table, Jaguar TCS Racing carries TCS as title partner, Castrol and Jaguar itself, and no fleet, mobility or ride-hail partner; nor does any other Formula E roster. Official Fleet Partner is a clean category.

why_team.label: Platform that lasts
why_team.text: Jaguar has committed to the GEN4 era, Seasons 13-16 through 2030, so a three-year deal sits inside a confirmed programme, and the London E-Prix is the team's home round in the city where Moove's next launch happens.

why_team.label: Road-to-race proof
why_team.text: Jaguar's Formula E programme exists to sell electric road cars; tens of thousands of driverless I-PACE hours a week in three cities is the most visible real-world use of that car anywhere, and Moove is the operator.

value.label: Halo with mechanics (Mode B)
value.text: Depots and charging orchestration are not a race-car input, and the brief says so. The value is commercial: a Jaguar-branded robotaxi story during race weeks at Miami and London, rider-to-race activations where Waymo riders are taken to the E-Prix in the cars, and a road-EV proof point the racing programme was built to promote.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Moove's investors and partners, Mubadala, Toyota's Woven Capital, Uber and Waymo, are the mobility and sovereign-capital audience Jaguar's other partners want in the suite at Miami and London.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: Driver appearances at Nest openings, a depot-to-grid content series on charging and energy management, and a reference story Moove can use with every city regulator it approaches.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Fleet Partner designation, sidepod placement, hospitality at the Miami and London rounds, rights to co-brand I-PACE fleet livery on race weeks, driver and engineering access for Moove's channels.

ruled_out.reason: US team with Miami and Austin rounds, but no vehicle tie; TWG AI and Quest Global fill its technology lanes.
Penske Autosport's parent runs its own truck-leasing and fleet businesses; a fleet operator on that car conflicts with the owner.

ruled_out.team: Nissan Formula E Team · Citroën Racing · Porsche Formula E Team · Cupra Kiro
ruled_out.reason: Manufacturer teams whose road cars are not in Moove's Waymo fleets; a Jaguar-fleet operator would sit awkwardly on a rival OEM's car.
Mahindra makes ride-hail vehicles in India, one of Moove's markets; the owner competes with Moove's suppliers.
Open but not chosen: no vehicle, city or partner tie comparable to Jaguar's.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Ladi Delano before Jaguar closes its Season 13 roster to agree a London E-Prix announcement window and size an Official Fleet Partner entry built around the Miami and London rounds.

# Moove → Jaguar TCS Racing — verification log (N° 151, issued for 5 Aug 2026)

Built in-session on 6 Sep 2026 at no API cost (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), with Claude as scanner, verifier and writer through the pipeline's injectable stages; the calendar table, sponsor table, 13-rule audit and 2-page render ran as code. The thin row's source was an aggregator (finsmes.com); the primary source is the lead investor's release on mubadala.com, mirrored on BusinessWire.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** mubadala.com, businesswire.com, techcrunch.com and finance.yahoo.com were egress-blocked; every claim was checked against search summaries of the primary page named in the evidence. The trigger is confirmed by a Tier-1 investor release plus four independent outlets, so confidence is HIGH, but treat VERIFIED lines as REPORTED until a person opens the link.

## The trigger

Mubadala release (5 Aug 2026; BusinessWire, TechCrunch, The National, Just Auto same day): $250M Series C at $2.1B; lead Mubadala; co-leads Woven Capital and Ion Pacific; new BlueCrest and Sona Capital; existing BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton, Uber, Left Lane, Square Associates, The Latest Ventures, OPG Pension Plan. One correction to the row: 'Nest charging infrastructure' → Nests are robotics-first depots (charging is one function). Figures ($420M ARR, ~42,000 vehicles, 29 cities, 13 countries, 150 → 500 AV staff) are from the release as quoted by Global Fleet and ITWeb Africa.

## Decision path

Ladi Delano, Co-Founder & Co-CEO and chairman (Businessday NG; billionaires.africa 6 Aug 2026; LinkedIn). Jide Odunsi, Co-Founder & Co-CEO. Tayo Oyegunle, COO. Tingting Peng, Chief Capital, Strategy and Impact Officer. **No CMO is listed** on any source found. Both founders are UK-based; HQ Dubai (The National).

## Leadership ties

`none found` after checking Delano, Odunsi and Oyegunle for F1 / FE / motorsport sponsorship history.

## Team fit

Judged only against `seeds/sponsors.json`: no fleet / mobility / ride-hail partner at Jaguar TCS Racing or on any FE roster. `data/teams.json` lists a 'financial services (Chase)' lock at Jaguar; Moove is pitched as a mobility-infrastructure brand, not a financial-services one, so the lock is noted, not triggered. Jaguar's GEN4 commitment (Seasons 13-16) from Jaguar Racing media. Waymo–Moove Phoenix/Miami (TechCrunch, Dec 2024) and London (Waymo blog, Oct 2025) are the strategic hook; the London commercial launch is *pending regulators* (TfL, Aug 2026) and the brief says so.

## Not claimed

- Reports that Moove also operates for Waymo in Las Vegas and a 2025 $1.2B debt raise appear only in AV trade blogs and are not used.
- Deal size ($1.5-2.5M a year) is an ESTIMATE.
- MODE B is stated honestly: Moove's product is not a race-team input.
- No post-trigger material event found between 5 Aug and 6 Sep 2026.
